description.value: The study examined whether Parkinson’s disease is associated with reduced insula functional connectivity and whether insula connectivity differs between depressed and non-depressed patients with Parkinson’s disease.

design.value: Two groups of PD patients, with and without depression, and a group of age- and sex-matched normal controls underwent resting-state BOLD fMRI. Seed-based functional connectivity maps were compared among the groups using general linear models with age and sex as covariates.

task_description.value: Anatomical images were acquired after the functional imaging.

description.value: Blood oxygenation level dependent (BOLD) images were acquired using an echo planar imaging sequence. TR = 2000ms, TE = 30ms, flip angle = 90°, FOV = 240 × 240mm2, matrix = 64 × 64, slice thickness = 5 mm, slice gap = 1 mm, 23 interleaved axial slices. A total of 185 resting-state BOLD images were acquired from each subject.
3-D GRE T1-weighted sequence, TR/TE = 5.14ms/1.17 ms, FOV = 240 × 240mm2, matrix = 256 × 256, slice thickness = 1.2mm; no gap, 124 sagittal slices.

The first 10 images were excluded. Remaining images were corrected for slice timing, realigned, nuisance covariates were regressed out, normalized into standard space using DARTEL and resampled to 3 × 3 × 3 mm voxel size, smoothed using a 6-mm Gaussian kernel, detrended, and bandpass filtered.

software.value: Data Processing Assistant for Resting-State fMRI (DPARSF)
Resting-State fMRI Data Analysis Toolkit (REST V1.8)

steps.value: The first 10 images were excluded from the analysis.
Corrected for slice timing using the middle slice as a reference.
Friston-24 head motion parameters and white matter and CSF signals calculated using the CompCor method were regressed out.
Normalized into the standard space using DARTEL and resampled to 3 × 3 × 3 mm voxel size.
Smoothed the images using a 6-mm Gaussian kernel.
Excluded subjects whose head motion exceeded 2 mm of translation or 2° of rotation.
Censored time points where FD > 0.5mm; subjects whose total length of data were <130 were excluded.

model_settings.value: Pearson’s correlation was calculated between the average time series within the ROIs and other brain areas. The resulting connectivity maps were transformed to Z maps using Fisher r-to-z transformation. Age and sex were used as covariates.
